chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī and another, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from a man, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, who said:

Honey and figs from Hamdān and Ḥulwān came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. He ordered the officials to bring the orphans, and he enabled them at the tops of the vessels to lick from them, while he was distributing it to the people cup by cup. Then it was said to him, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, why are they licking it?” He said, “Indeed, the Imam is the father of the orphans, and I only let them lick this out of the care of fathers.”

key_terms.أَبُو الْيَتَامَى: father of the orphans, meaning guardian and caretaker of them
key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amīr al-Muʾminīn, the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the Imam, the divinely appointed leader
key_terms.الْعُرَفَاءَ: the officials or supervisors entrusted with carrying out instructions
key_terms.الْيَتَامَى: the orphans, children lacking a father’s care
key_terms.بِرِعَايَةِ الْآبَاءِ: with the care of fathers, indicating paternal compassion and guardianship

ai.seo_question: How does Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام describe the Imam’s responsibility toward orphans?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident in which Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام showed special tenderness toward orphans while distributing provisions to the people. It highlights the Imam’s paternal care for the vulnerable and presents leadership as including compassion, guardianship, and attention to those without protectors.
